title: Sinus bradycardia
summary: The sinus node fires too slowly. Conduction is normal; only the rate is abnormal.

events.label: Sinus node
events.caption: The sinus node fires, but slowly: here once every 1.4 seconds, about 43 times a minute.

events.label: Normal conduction
events.caption: The impulse follows the usual route, so the PR interval and the narrow QRS are normal.
events.ecg: Every P wave is followed by a QRS: this is sinus rhythm, only slow.

events.label: Long wait
events.caption: A long pause before the next beat. The only abnormality is the rate, below 60 per minute.
events.ecg: Long flat intervals between normal complexes.

teaching_points: Sinus bradycardia is sinus rhythm with a rate below 60 per minute; check that the P wave axis is normal (slide 22).
Causes include vagal tone, athletes, drugs (beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers, digoxin, amiodarone), sinus node disease and ischaemia (slide 23).
Bradycardia comes from reduced automaticity or from conduction block (slide 17).
